== Overview ==

Geisha is the service which provides the user interface for the Wii U eShop. The eShop application is actually a custom web browser which loads https://ninja.wup.shop.nintendo.net/ninja/wood_index.html, which redirects to https://geisha-wup.cdn.nintendo.net/geisha/index.html. The interface is built using standard HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The browser also exposes several custom JavaScript APIs in order for the application to perform system/eShop related actions, such as getting user details from the console or starting a title download.

<div style="background-color: rgb(234, 243, 255); border-color: rgb(163, 202, 255); border-style: solid; border-width: 1px; color: rgb(32, 33, 34); max-width: 800px; width: fit-content;">
<div style="background-color: rgb(203, 214, 246); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; height: 24px; line-height: 24px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 5px; padding-left: 20px;">Note</div>
<div style="padding: 5px;">''The 3DS does not load a web page from the internet for it's user interface. This page is only relevant for the Wii U.''</div>
</div>

== Limitations ==

The eShop browser is based on [https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/tree/safari-536.28-branch WebKit 536.28], which was released in 2013. Nintendo also made several modifications to it's fork of WebKit, which can be found here https://support.nintendo.com/jp/oss/index.html. Because of the browsers age and custom changes by Nintendo, it should '''''NOT''''' be assumed that any modern frameworks, tools, etc. will work on it. Careful consideration needs to be made when writing client-side code for this browser to ensure that a given feature is implemented, and implemented well (even if a feature is technicaly available in normal releases of [https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/tree/safari-536.28-branch WebKit 536.28], Nintendo may have removed them or changed how they behave).

Useful resources:

* Work towards a dedicated browser all that uses these custom/older versions of WebKit for debugging off-device: https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/org-issues/issues/5
* Work towards a custom framework for making modern feeling web apps for Nintendo's browser apps: https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/Yeah/pull/1

== Whitelist ==

The eShop browser utilizes a whitelist which dictates the browser is allowed to load assets from. If the browser tries to load assets from a server/path not in this whitelist, or not from the current domain, the request will fail. This whitelist is sent to the console in the <code>X-Nintendo-Whitelist</code> response header when loading the page UI. The whitelist has the following structure. The parser for this header is located at <code>0x02102660</code> in the eShop (USA v131) <code>wave.rpx</code>. The latest official whitelist is:

<pre>
1|https,wiiu-ssl-static.ubi.com,,6|https,nintendojp.d1.sc.omtrdc.net,,2|https,nintendojp.tt.omtrdc.net,,2|https,admin8.testandtarget.omniture.com,,2|https,www.googletagmanager.com,,2|https,www.google-analytics.com,,2|https,kanzashi-wup.cdn.nintendo.net,,2|https,kanzashi-movie-wup.cdn.nintendo.net,,2|https,kanzashi-qa.wup.shop.nintendo.net,,2|https,kanzashi-movie-qa.wup.shop.nintendo.net,,2
</pre>

=== Whitelist ===

{| class="wikitable"
! Field !! Description
|-
| Version number? || Always <code>1</code>. Parser bails if this value is not <code>1</code>
|-
| Entries || List of [[#Whitelist Entry]] configurations. Any number of configurations can be set
|}

=== Whitelist Entry ===

Entries defined later in the list take priority over earlier entires. This can be useful if, for example, a developer wanted to be able to loosely use any subdomain via an earlier defined wild card that can serve on any path, but then restrict a specific subdomain to a specific path.

{| class="wikitable"
! Field !! Description
|-
| Scheme || The protocol scheme the client will use when connecting to the server (<code>https</code>, <code>http</code>, etc.)
|-
| Host || The domain name being whitelisted. Max length of 128 bytes. 3 "modes" are available. Modes cannot be mixed together, each entry can only use one mode, though a domain can have multiple entries. Modes are checked for in this order: Mode 1 = "any subdomain", enabled by a leading period. This works for any depth. For example <code>.example.com</code> will allow both <code>subdomain.example.com</code> and <code>deeply.nested.subdomain.example.com</code>, but not <code>example.com</code> itself (this requires an additional mode 3 entry). Mode 2 = "any TLD", enabled by a trailing period. For example <code>example.</code> will allow both <code>example.com</code> and <code>example.org</code>. Mode 3 = "exact match", enabled by having no trailing/leading periods. For example, the following entries allows both the main YouTube domain and all subdomains <code>https,youtube.com,,2&#124;https,.youtube.com,,2</code>
|-
| Path || The path (including the leading slash) content can be served by for this domain. Max length of 128 bytes. If left empty, any path is accepted
|-
| Flags || Set as a hex string. Only flags <code>(flags >> 1) & 1</code> and <code>(flags >> 2) & 1</code> are extracted by the parser, purpose unknown. The first flag seems to always be set in official whitelists?
|}

== Localizations ==

The eShop supports localizing the interface by loading various localization files. These are XML documents containing translation keys to replace in the interface.

<div style="background-color: rgb(234, 243, 255); border-color: rgb(163, 202, 255); border-style: solid; border-width: 1px; color: rgb(32, 33, 34); max-width: 800px; width: fit-content;">
<div style="background-color: rgb(203, 214, 246); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; height: 24px; line-height: 24px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 5px; padding-left: 20px;">Note</div>
<div style="padding: 5px;">''Since only the Wii U uses Geisha, and it can be an entirely custom web application, it is not required that any custom implementations implement localizations this way. This is documented for historical and convention purposes.''</div>
</div>

<pre>

  <entry key="localization_key2">Localized String 2</entry>
  ...
</properties>
</pre>

== JavaScript APIs ==

Since the interface is entirely customized by whatever Geisha provides, this page will mainly focus document the custom JavaScript APIs used by the eShop. Each API provides a specialized set of functions the client can invoke to handle tasks such as interacting with the system, querying for account details, etc. Many of these APIs can be found in other browser-based applications on Nintendo Network, such as [[Online/Nintendo_Network/Miiverse|Miiverse]] and [[Online/Nintendo_Network/TVii|TVii]], however this page will only cover what is available to the Wii U eShop.

Since the Wii U eShop is a web application, TypeScript types for these APIs, and the APIs found in other browser-based applications, can be found at https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/applet-types.

See https://hackmd.io/@quarky/Bkbr1cJ2P for how the APIs are registered. '''''Note:''''' ''This page is not specific to the eShop, and thus may have information that does not apply to it.''

== wiiuEC ==

Handles e-commerce related tasks.

=== <code>wiiuEC.needsSystemUpdate()</code> ===

Checks if the console needs a system update.

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>{ update: boolean; }</code> || Whether a system update is required
|}

=== <code>wiiuEC.needsSystemUpdateUsingCache()</code> ===

Checks if the console needs a system update using cached data.

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>{ update: boolean; }</code> || Whether a system update is required
|}

=== <code>wiiuEC.getECommerceInfraStatus()</code> ===

Checks if the infrastructure to install titles is available. Triggers [[Online/Nintendo_Network/SOAP/ecs#GetStandbyMode|ecs:GetStandbyMode]].

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>{ isStandby: boolean; } &#124; { error: { code: number; }; }</code> || An object containing the result <code>ServiceStandbyMode</code> on success, or an object containing an error code on failure
|}

=== <code>wiiuEC.getDeviceCountry()</code> ===

Gets the devices registered country.

{| class="wikitable"

_addAppJumpEvent: function() {
  var a = this.sessionStorage.getItem("analytics_appjump");
  if (!a)

  "caffeine_killer" === a.launcherType && this._addEvent("kntf", {

}

== wiiuNNA ==

Used to manage data about the currently logged in Nintendo Network ID ('''N'''intendo '''N'''etwork '''A'''ccount).

=== <code>wiiuNNA.principalId</code> ===

Read-only property. The current user's Nintendo Network ID PID.

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Description
|-
| <code>string</code> || The user's NNID PID
|}

=== <code>wiiuNNA.principalIdHashKey</code> ===

Read-only property. Salt used when hashing the current user's PID. Official implementation:

<pre>
getHashedPID: function() {
  if (!b)
    return d.getItem("pid") || "00000000000000000000000000000000";
  var a = parseInt(wiiuNNA.principalId, 10);
  a = isNaN(a) ? "0" : a.toString(16);
  a = ["00000000", a].join("");
  a = a.substr(a.length - 8);
  a = [wiiuNNA.principalIdHashKey, a].join("");
  return jQuery().crypt({
    method: "md5",
    source: a
  })
}
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Description
|-
| <code>string</code> || <code>GvXfcxbp8lvp0zwbKvqZtitwqckFyuqB</code>
|}

== wiiuNfc ==

Manages the GamePad NFC reader, for (Japanese only?) card payments on the GamePad.

=== <code>NFCMessageType</code> ===

<pre>
enum NFCMessageType {
  NONE = 0,
  CANCEL_PROHIBIT = 1,
  NETWORK_ERROR = 2,
  UNDER_MAINTENANCE_ERROR = 3,
  DEVICE_POLLING_START = 10,
  DEVICE_DETECT_CARD = 11,
  DEVICE_TOUCH_AGAIN = 12,
  DEVICE_TOUCH_DIFF_CARD = 13,
  PAYMENT_RESPONSE = 20,
  BALANCE_INQUIRY_RESPONSE = 21,
  RESULT_CHECK_RESPONSE = 22,
  HISTORY_INQUIRY_RESPONSE = 23
}
</pre>

=== <code>wiiuNfc.startPolling()</code> ===

Starts NFC polling. Will continue to poll for messages (checkable with [[#wiiuNfc.getMessage()]]) until [[#wiiuNfc.cancel()]] is called.

{| class="wikitable"
! Parameter !! Type !! Description
|-
| <code>type</code> || <code>number</code> || The NFC operation type. Known values: 1 (payment), 3 (balance inquiry), 5 (history inquiry), 9 (result check)
|-
| <code>unknown</code> || <code>string</code> || Unknown
|}

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>{ error?: { code: number; }; }</code> || An empty object on success, or an object containing an error code on failure
|}

=== <code>wiiuNfc.cancel()</code> ===

Ends NFC polling.

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>boolean</code> || Unknown
|}

=== <code>wiiuNfc.getMessage()</code> ===

Gets the latest message type.

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>NFCMessageType</code> || Message type
|}

=== <code>wiiuNfc.getResponse()</code> ===

Gets the response from the NFC reader. Only usable when [[#wiiuNfc.getMessage()]] is one of <code>PAYMENT_RESPONSE</code>, <code>BALANCE_INQUIRY_RESPONSE</code>, <code>RESULT_CHECK_RESPONSE</code> or <code>HISTORY_INQUIRY_RESPONSE</code>.

{| class="wikitable"
! Parameter !! Type !! Description
|-
| <code>messageType</code> || <code>NFCMessageType</code> || Message type
|}

{| class="wikitable"
! Return Type !! Description
|-
| <code>{ isSuccess: boolean; message: string; result_code: number; }</code> || NFC response data
|}

Opens the page <code>/communities/4294967295?title_id=<TITLE_ID_AS_DECIMAL>&src=lib</code> if <code>titleID</code> is a hex encoded UInt32 value.
